title: "Resources"
order: 105
---

This module cites no AABB Standards text — QSE (Quality System Essential) 4 is named and
themed only, the same handling this curriculum gives every AABB Standard. The links below
are AABB's own public pages describing the framework this module's tiering scheme sits
under, plus the internal-course link back to the incident this module's running example
reuses. All were checked and loading at the time this page was written.

- **[AABB: Updated Quality Systems Essentials](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/about-aabb-standards/updated-quality-systems-essentials)**
  — AABB's own public page confirming the ten-element Quality System Essentials structure
  (QSE 4 is "Supplier and Customer Issues," the element this module applies) and that all
  current AABB Standards are built on this template. Read it for the structure, not a
  specific standard number — this page doesn't enumerate the ten element titles itself.

- **[AABB: Proposed 34th Edition of *Standards for Blood Banks and Transfusion
  Services*](https://www.aabb.org/docs/default-source/default-document-library/standards/proposed-34th-edition-of-standards-for-blood-banks-and-transfusion-services.pdf?sfvrsn=8d0d4f7b_0)**
  (PDF) — a proposed, comment-period edition, not confirmed as currently adopted text, but
  the clearest publicly available document naming all ten QSE-aligned chapters, including
  "Suppliers and Customers." Useful if you want to see the supplier-and-customer element
  named inside an actual (proposed) Standards document, rather than taking this lesson's
  paraphrase on faith. Do not cite a chapter or standard number from this PDF as current,
  adopted AABB text — it's a comment-period draft.

- **[Investigating a Healthcare Data Incident](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/investigating-a-healthcare-data-incident/index.qmd)**
  — the final module of `healthcare-security-and-privacy`, where the device-management
  platform vendor, the Brookfield laptop, and the permanently unresolved encryption
  question were all first established. Read it (or re-read it) before module 2 — this
  course's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 modules assume you remember exactly what that investigation
  did and didn't resolve.
